transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I'm just so tired. It's like my body is filled with wet sand. I can barely get through a shift at work right now, and even when I do rest, it doesn't really help. I just never feel like I'm getting any energy back.
Along with feeling so exhausted, have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless?

I don't really think so. I mean, I haven't been crying or feeling like things are hopeless or anything like that. It's really just the exhaustion. I don't feel sad, I just... I just feel completely drained of energy.
How long have you been experiencing this level of exhaustion?

It's been about four months now. This low, empty feeling has just... dragged on. It started a while after I had this big rush of energy at work, but that passed a long time ago. Now it's just the exhaustion.
During that time when you had that rush of energy, did you feel like you needed much less sleep than usual?

Yeah, exactly. With the changing shifts at work, I got to a point where I'd sleep only a few hours and still feel completely wired. I didn't even feel tired back then. And the weird thing is, now, even when I’m this exhausted, I still wake up early with my mind already going.
Have you noticed a loss of interest or pleasure in doing things you normally enjoy?

Yeah, I have. Things I usually love doing just feel... flat now. Like, I used to enjoy cooking for myself, playing my guitar, going hiking, or even just heading over to my family's place. But lately, when I do any of that, it feels like I'm just going through the motions. I'm only pretending to care about it.
During that time when you had all that extra energy, did your thoughts feel like they were racing or jumping quickly from one idea to another?

Yeah, they really did. It was like my thoughts were just jumping so fast. I'd be thinking about getting a promotion at work, and then right away my brain is on how to fix the store layout, and then it's on my bills, or... things I should buy. It was just going and going. I couldn't even grab onto one idea long enough to actually finish it.
How long did that period of high energy last?
I'm not really sure, to be honest. It's hard to put a number on it. It just kind of... happened for a while, and then it didn't. I didn't really keep track of the days or anything.
During that period of high energy, did it cause any significant problems with your work or personal life?

Yeah, it really did. At work... well, I'm a cashier, and I started making mistakes on the register. I was also falling behind on my tasks in the cash office. It got bad enough that my manager actually took me off some of my responsibilities, which really sucked because I was hoping those extra duties would help me get a promotion. And in my personal life, I've just been avoiding my family completely. It actually got to the point where I needed to get same-day crisis help recently, because I... I just didn't feel safe trying to handle it all by myself.
